Across validation windows the model ranking is unstable (Kendall tau 0.033), which favours a robust combination.

attempts.rationale: The series shows strong trend/seasonality but ranking is unstable, so a robust weighted combo is sensible.
Test a weighted combo that uses inverse_error weights to see if error‑based weighting outperforms the softmax approach on this highly seasonal, trend‑driven series.
The series shows strong trend and seasonality but ranking is unstable; a simple robust mean may compete with weighted combos.

The series has strong trend and seasonality, but ranking is unstable and several models share correlated errors. A trimmed mean can be a robust alternative to weighted combos and may reduce influence of outliers.
test a different kind of strategy – a deterministic blend (dba) on the reduced, low‑error pool to see if a more aggressive optimization improves over trimmed mean.

The unstable ranking and strong seasonality suggest a robust DBA on the full pool may beat trimmed_mean.
try a robust median on the stable pool4 to see if trimming improves over mean/trimmed_mean.
Test a simple mean over the stable pool4 to see if a non‑robust average can beat trimmed_mean given the strong seasonality and trend.

decision.justification: Selected 'trimmed_mean' (an agent proposal) as the best of 11 backtested attempts, score 0.7789. Series context: trend strength 0.9993 and seasonal strength 1.0; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.033); 10 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 2.835.
